Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

prepare verb

get oneself ready

also get ready, be ready, prepare for

classical

Liv. 21.31.1: ad iter sē parāre jubet

sē parāre

verb, first conjugation, reflexive; with ad and the accusative, or an infinitive

get ready, prepare oneself

For what is coming: ad iter sē parāre, to get ready for the journey.

Other words

  • sē comparāre — make oneself ready

    verb, first conjugation, reflexive; with ad and the accusative · also used · classical · Liv. 28.33.1 (Lewis & Short): sē ad iter; Cic. Mil. 28 (Lewis & Short)

  • parātus, parāta, parātum — ready

    adjective (participle of parō), declension · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.7.11: ego vērō sum parātus

    With ad and the accusative, or an infinitive: ready for, ready to.

Examples

  • corpora cūrāre atque ad iter sē parāre jubet

    He tells them to eat and rest and get ready for the march.Liv. 21.31.1

  • custōs ut sīs līminis, ā fūribus tueāris et noctū domum. — ego vērō sum parātus

    “Just guard the door and keep the house safe from thieves at night.” — “I’m ready for that, all right.”Phaedr. 3.7.9–11

  • Parā tē; jam proficīscimur.

    Get ready; we’re leaving now.composed

See also prepare, pack.

SourcesLewis & Short: paro · Lewis & Short: comparo · Lewis & Short: paratus
